_about.purpose: Movement rows for the Tier 1/2/3 rules in Company_TopChemical_Actions.js (BOX_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md §7).
_about.READ_THIS_FIRST: EVERY ROW HERE IS SYNTHETIC. Not one of them came from the production table. They were constructed to make a specific rule fire, or — just as important — to make sure it does NOT. They prove the rules do what they say on data whose answer is known; they say nothing about how often any of this occurs in the live table, and nothing about the false-positive rate on real data. That measurement needs DB access and is a blocked-on-owner item in NEXT_STEPS_OWNER.md.
_about.shape: Columns match regular_box_movement. `parse` is NOT stored — the test runs the real parser over transaction_details, so a parser change cannot leave a stale rule fixture behind.
_about.expect: rule ids that MUST fire for the row, and must_not for ids that must not.
_about.groups: Rules INTERACT — a duplicate-pair fixture is also a row in the id/date sequence, and a fixture written to exercise one rule will trip another by accident. So each row carries a `group`, and the checks run the engine once PER GROUP. Within a group the wording and amounts are deliberately made distinct unless the rule under test needs them alike, so a scenario tests one thing. There is also one run over ALL rows, which asserts only that nothing crashes and that every flag produced is explainable.
_about.note_on_populations: BACKDATED needs n>=30 and STRUCTURING needs a histogram, so those two are exercised against populations the test GENERATES from a documented recipe rather than listing 60 rows here. The recipe is in tools/verify/box_rules.js and is printed when the check runs.

id and date both advance. Normal. It is an INTERIOR row, so it is genuinely tested — the first and last rows of a set are skipped by the rule.
